title: Release rhythm & cut-criteria playbook for API | Console | Runtime
creator: Emily Zhang
description: One-page playbook and checklist to synchronize milestones, scope locks, cut criteria, release-notes coordination, and cross-team go-to-market tasks across API, Console, and Runtime. Intention: provide a single source-of-truth for the next release window that engineering, design, docs, security, support, and GTM can follow to avoid last-minute surprises.
context: We are converging several change streams this quarter (runtime perf changes, console UX updates, and API semantics tweaks). Historically coordination gaps have caused last-minute scope cuts and inconsistent release notes. This playbook documents rules-of-the-road (milestones + cut criteria) and an ownership matrix for release notes and customer communications.
goals: Define clear milestone cadence and enforce scope-lock rules across API, Console, Runtime
Ensure release notes are generated, reviewed, and published in a single canonical doc with per-team sections
Minimize emergency post-GA fixes by baking in performance and quality gates before cut
Coordinate GTM artifacts (release blog, changelog, status page, marketplace manifests) with at least 5 business days notice
milestones: M0 - Kickoff: Align owners, runbook, and high-level scope (2026-02-18)
M1 - Feature window close / scope lock candidate list due (2026-03-01)
M2 - Docs & SDKs draft ready (docs freeze candidate) (2026-03-10)
M3 - Performance & SLO verification window (runtime canary) (2026-03-15 to 2026-03-22)
M4 - Release candidate + internal signoffs (security, legal, support) (2026-03-24)
M5 - GA rollout (staged) - API hosted -> Dedicated -> Private (target 2026-03-26)
M6 - Post-GA monitoring and 7-day stabilization window (2026-03-26 to 2026-04-02)
scope_lock_criteria: All P0 acceptance tests (API contracts, Console critical paths, runtime p95) green in canary
Telemetry coverage: token-level latency, error rates, and request tracing enabled for new code paths
Security signoff: no open critical/high vulnerabilities and threat-model artifacts reviewed
Docs/Samples: migration notes and SDK examples present for any customer-facing change
Rollback plan: validated deploy + rollback playbook with runbook owner listed
cut_criteria: Any regression causing >=1.5x increase in P95 latency on a representative trace sample -> cut the change
Open P0 (severity) bugs blocking core API or Console flows -> scope cut until fixed
Failed canary with error budget burn above threshold -> postpone GA
Major breaking change lacking automated migration path documented -> delay or move to opt-in
Missed security review sign-off or outstanding compliance items -> do not release
release_notes_plan: Canonical release-notes doc (Confluence) maintained by PM; per-team sections (API, Console, Runtime, Docs, Breaking changes)
Template required fields: summary, migration steps, example snippet, owner, risk level, public vs internal
Change taxonomy: Major (breaking), Minor (behavioral), Patch (bugfix); tag entries accordingly
PR owners must include a 'release-notes' entry in the PR template; CI checklist will fail if missing
Review cadence: Draft by docs team by M2, PM review by M3, Final review 48h before RC cut
Changelog generation: automated script pulls tags from canonical doc to produce the GitHub release and blog draft
go_to_market_tasks: GTM owner to prepare public blog draft and product demo by M3
Prepare customer-facing migrate checklist and SDK migration examples
Update status page and incident playbook entries for new behavior (GTM + SRE)
Coordinate marketplace/partner listing updates (if applicable) with partners 7 business days prior
Sales enablement: one-pager with talking points + known limitations distributed 3 days before GA
Support enablement: run a 60-minute walkthrough of new features and runbooks with Level 1/2 teams
risks: Late-breaking performance regressions in runtime leading to scope cuts
Insufficient telemetry causing missed regressions until GA
Docs lag: SDK/docs not updated in time for GA causing customer confusion
Cross-team calendar conflicts reduce review bandwidth in final week
Private deployment edge-cases (on-prem) not exercised in canary
decisions: Adopt staggered GA: hosted API first for faster rollback, Dedicated next, then Private after appliance validation
Enforce a hard scope-freeze except for security fixes after M1 unless PM approves exceptions
Use the canonical Confluence doc as the single source-of-truth for release notes; auto-generate GitHub release from that doc
Require security signoff for any change touching customer keys, networking, or audit logs
